newsitem.title: UK: IATA says SE Asian airfreight to grow 17 pct a yr.
newsitem.headline: IATA says SE Asian airfreight to grow 17 pct a yr.

text.p: Airfreight within the south-east Asian region is forecast grow by an annual average growth rate of 17 percent between end 1995 and 2000, the International Air Transport Association (IATA) said.
In its annual five year forecast, due to be published later this year, IATA said this represents overall growth for the period of 119.7 percent.

Other regions which will see strong growth are north-east Asia to south Asia (the Indian sub-continent) with an annual average growth rate of 12.6 percent, up a total of 81.1 percent for the five years, it added.
There will be also a substantial growth averaging 10.9 percent a year in airfreight from south Asia to south-east Asia, the forecast said.
South Asia to western Europe will show an average annual gain of 9.6 percent or 58.4 percent between end-1995 and 2000
Airfreight trade within the north-east Asian region will rise at an average annual rate of 8.3 percent, up 49 percent overall.
North-east Asian airfreight to south-east Asia will rise at an annual 10 percent rate, or 61.1 percent over the IATA forecast shows.
Higher growth is expected in air trade to both central and eastern Europe as well as southern Africa, but the base date makes it difficult to provide a firm forecast, IATA added.
On western Europe to lower Latin America ( Argentina, Brazil and Chile )routes, airfreight volumes will grow at 6.6 percent or 37.6 percent for the five years, IATA added.
